title: Balanced and Unbalanced Forces
seo_title: Grade 3 Forces Worksheets: Balanced and Unbalanced Forces, Pushes and Pulls
standard_text: Plan and conduct an investigation to provide evidence of the effects of balanced and unbalanced forces on the motion of an object.
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 science worksheets on balanced and unbalanced forces (NGSS 3-PS2-1): pushes and pulls, force arrows, tug-of-war and how forces change motion. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Unbalanced forces change motion. Balanced forces do not.
key_sub: A force is a push or a pull. Equal and opposite forces are balanced, so the object keeps doing what it was doing.
body_html:
How to think about it

A force is a push or a pull. Forces have a size and a direction. We show them with arrows: a longer arrow means a bigger force.

Balanced forces are equal and opposite. They do not change how an object moves. Unbalanced forces are not equal. They make an object start, stop, speed up, slow down or change direction.

Example

In a tug-of-war, both teams pull equally hard. What happens?

The pulls are equal and opposite.

The forces are balanced.

Answer: The rope does not move.

Example

A ball at rest is kicked. Are the forces balanced?

The ball starts moving.

Motion changed.

Answer: No, they are unbalanced.

Common mistakes

  • Thinking an object at rest has no forces. The forces are balanced.
  • Thinking the object moves toward the smaller force. It moves in the direction of the bigger force.
  • Saying “balanced” means there are no forces.

faq.q: What is the difference between balanced and unbalanced forces?
faq.a: Balanced forces are equal and opposite and do not change motion. Unbalanced forces are not equal and make an object start, stop, speed up, slow down or turn.

faq.q: Are there forces on an object that is not moving?
faq.a: Yes. Gravity pulls it down and the floor or table pushes it up. The forces are balanced.

faq.q: Which way does an object move when forces are unbalanced?
faq.a: It moves in the direction of the bigger force.
